text: My recruiter in Dhaka told me I owe 180,000 taka before I can get my Qatar visa. He says this is normal for construction workers and I have to pay or lose my slot. Is this legal?

I arrived in Dubai three weeks ago but my employer still has my passport. He said he will return it after six months when my probation period ends. My friend said this is standard here — is that true?

The agency in Chittagong promised me a factory supervisor job in Saudi Arabia at 1,200 SAR per month. When I landed in Riyadh the contract showed 700 SAR and the job is cleaning toilets. My sponsor says I signed the local contract and the original does not matter. What can I do?

I am working in Kuwait as a household helper. Madam has not paid me for four months and says the unpaid months are to cover the placement fee she paid the agency. Is she allowed to deduct that from my salary?

My kafeel in Bahrain will not let me change employers even though he has not paid me since Eid. He says my visa is tied to him and if I leave I will be deported and blacklisted. Is there any way out under the new labour reforms?

Before flying to Oman I paid 2,500 USD to a sub-agent in Sylhet. He gave me a receipt but the main agency in Dhaka denies receiving any money and says I still owe them 1,000 USD more. Both are threatening to cancel my visa. I have no more savings. What should I do?

I came to the UAE on a visit visa and the agent here converted it to a work visa under a company I have never heard of. Now the real employer says I am working illegally and threatens to report me unless I pay him 500 AED each month as protection money. Can he do this?

Rashida from my village came back from Qatar after two years and said she was never allowed to go outside alone. The family took her phone on arrival and only gave it back on the day she left. She was paid but could not contact her family for months at a time. Is that a normal domestic worker situation?

My work permit in Saudi Arabia is under a free-visa arrangement. My actual boss is a subcontractor and the sponsor name on my iqama is someone I have never met. Last week a government inspector came and said I am working illegally. Am I at risk of deportation even though I have a valid iqama stamp?

The recruitment company in Comilla advertised a hotel waiter job in Dubai at 1,500 AED. They asked for a training fee of 50,000 taka and said it covers a three-day food-hygiene course and visa processing. After I paid, they told me the job is now a dishwasher role at 900 AED. Can I get my training fee back?
My recruiter in Addis collected 45,000 birr before I could get my Qatar visa. He said it covers 'processing and placement' but gave me no receipt. Is this normal or am I being cheated?

I am a domestic worker in Riyadh and my employer took my Ethiopian passport on the first day. She says she will keep it for 'safekeeping' until my two-year contract ends. What can I do to get it back?

Selam here. I signed a contract in Addis that said 3,500 SAR per month cleaning offices in Jeddah. When I arrived my new employer showed me a different contract — 1,800 SAR and twelve-hour shifts, six days a week. The agency back home is not answering my calls.

My kafeel in Dubai owes me four months of unpaid wages. Every time I ask he threatens to report me to immigration for 'absconding'. I am scared to go to the police. Is there any authority that can help without deporting me?

A woman from my village left for Bahrain six months ago through an agent named Tadesse. We heard she is locked inside the house and not allowed to go to church on Fridays or contact family. Her employer also confiscated her phone. How do we report this from Ethiopia?

I want to go to Kuwait as a cleaner. The agent is asking me to pay 60,000 birr up front and says I will earn it back in the first three months. My cousin says this is a scam. Can you explain the legal maximum fee in Ethiopia for outbound domestic workers?

Almaz here. I have been working in an Omani household for eight months. My madam docks 200 rial from my salary every month, saying it is to repay my 'airfare loan' and agency commission. My original contract said the employer covers all these costs. Is this legal?

I applied through a licensed Addis Ababa agency called Birhan Staffing for a hotel job in Abu Dhabi. But when I landed I was taken to a private villa and told I would work as a housemaid instead. The hotel contract I signed in Ethiopia does not exist here. What are my rights?

My Saudi sponsor says I need his written permission — an 'exit visa' — before I can leave the country even for a family emergency back home. I have been here two years and my contract is finished. Can he really stop me from boarding a plane?

Someone online is offering Ethiopian girls a 'housekeeping supervisor' role in Qatar paying 5,000 QAR with free accommodation. They ask for nothing up front but say we must hand over our passports to the Doha office on arrival for 'visa registration'. Should I trust this offer?
My recruiter in Surabaya told me the RM 2,500 placement fee will be deducted from my first three months' salary once I start working in Kuala Lumpur. Is that normal or is something wrong?
I arrived in Johor Bahru last week and my employer took my passport for 'safekeeping.' They said it is standard practice here but I am not comfortable. What should I do?
Saya sudah bayar Rp 18 juta kepada agen di Medan sebelum berangkat ke Malaysia. Sekarang majikan bilang saya masih hutang RM 4,000 lagi untuk biaya visa dan transportasi. Apakah ini boleh?

My friend Dewi signed a contract in Bahasa Indonesia in Jakarta but when she arrived in Penang the employer showed her a different English contract with longer hours and lower pay. She is afraid to complain because her passport is held at the agency office.

I work as a domestic helper in Ampang and I have not been paid for two months. My employer says my wages are being held until my 'loan' from the maid agency is fully settled. The loan was supposed to be RM 1,800 but now they say it is RM 3,600. How do I report this?

A job ad on social media promised factory work in Shah Alam paying RM 1,500 a month with free housing. The recruiter in Bandung asked for Rp 5 million upfront and said I would get it back after three months. Now I am here and the pay is only RM 900 and they deduct RM 300 for dormitory. Is this legal?

I need to renew my PLKS work permit but my employer says I have to pay RM 700 myself even though my contract says the company covers permit costs. They are threatening to report me to immigration if I refuse. What are my rights?

Nama saya Ratna, saya kerja di kebun kelapa sawit di Sabah. Agen bilang gaji RM 1,200 tapi setiap bulan dipotong RM 500 untuk 'biaya penginapan dan makan' yang tidak pernah disebutkan di kontrak. Sudah 8 bulan dan saya tidak bisa keluar dari perkebunan karena tidak punya dokumen.

My sponsor in Kuala Lumpur changed my job from hotel cleaning to hostess work at a karaoke lounge without telling me before I left Indonesia. When I objected they said I owed them RM 5,000 in fees and could not leave until I paid. I managed to get to a friend's house. Who can help me?

I hold a valid visit pass but my broker arranged for me to work informally at a garment workshop in Petaling Jaya. The owner keeps my IC copy and says if I leave before six months he will report me as an illegal worker. I want to leave but I am scared. Is there a safe way out?
My recruiter in Hyderabad told me I owe 85,000 rupees for my visa and flight to Dubai before I can start work. He said I will pay it back from my salary over six months. Is this normal for Gulf jobs?

I am working as a domestic worker in Kuwait for two years now but my madam is keeping my passport. She says it is for safekeeping but I want to go home and she says I cannot leave until I find a replacement worker. What can I do?

The agency in Kerala promised me a job as a hotel receptionist in Qatar with 1,200 QAR monthly salary and free accommodation. When I arrived they took me to a cleaning company and said the hotel job was cancelled. Now my salary is 600 QAR and I share a room with eleven other men. Can I break the contract?

I paid 1.2 lakh rupees to a Punjabi agent for a visa to Saudi Arabia but after six months I still have no visa and the agent stopped answering calls. My family borrowed money for this and we are in debt. Is there any way to get a refund or report him?

My sponsor in Bahrain changed my job from driver to farm labourer without telling me. He says if I complain to the government he will cancel my iqama and I will be deported and blacklisted. I am scared. What are my rights?

I work in a garment factory in Ajman and my employer has not paid salary for three months. He says the company has cash flow problems and we must wait. We are not allowed to leave the labour camp without permission. Is this legal under UAE law?

A sub-agent told my cousin in Tamil Nadu that for 40,000 rupees he can get her a caregiver visa for Oman and she will earn 250 OMR per month. The agent asked for 20,000 upfront and the rest on arrival. I am worried this sounds suspicious. How do we check if the job is real?

I have been working in a restaurant in Riyadh for eight months. My employer told me my exit permit is linked to his approval and he will not sign the NOC unless I pay 5,000 SAR for training costs he says I owe him. I never signed anything about training fees. What can I do?

I came to Kuwait on a visit visa and a man at a shop connected me to a cleaning company that said they would regularise my status later. Now six months have passed, I am working without a valid work permit, they pay me 60 KWD instead of the 120 KWD promised, and they say if I leave they will report me to immigration. What should I do?

My building contractor in Dubai makes us work from 6am to 8pm six days a week in summer heat. When workers fainted last week he did not call a doctor. The accommodation is a shared dormitory with broken toilets. Can I file a complaint without losing my job or visa?

I am from Nairobi and an agent told me I will work as a housemaid in Dubai for 2,000 AED per month but first I must pay 45,000 KES for my visa processing and flight. Is this normal? My friend said she paid nothing when she went.

My employer in Riyadh has been holding my passport since I arrived three months ago. He says it is for safekeeping and I will get it back when my contract ends in two years. I am scared to ask for it because I need this job to pay back what I borrowed for my placement.

I signed a contract in Mombasa showing my salary as 1,800 AED for cleaning work in Abu Dhabi, but when I arrived my employer gave me a new contract for 1,200 AED and said if I refuse to sign I will be deported. What can I do?

My recruiter in Eldoret told me I would be a receptionist at a hotel in Qatar, but when I landed I was taken to a private house and told I must work as a housemaid. The agency back home is not answering my calls. I paid 60,000 KES to get here.

I have been in Muscat for eight months and my employer has not paid me for the last four months. He says I owe him for the flight, accommodation, and food and that I cannot leave until I clear the debt. Is this legal?

The lady who recruited me in Nakuru said my kafala sponsor in Jeddah is very good but I am not allowed to go outside the house alone or use my phone after 8pm. My sponsor reads all my messages. Is this normal for domestic workers in Saudi?

I want to go to Kuwait for work and a local agent says he can arrange everything for 80,000 KES which I would repay from my salary over six months. My salary would be 1,500 KWD per month. Should I trust this arrangement?

My sister is in Bahrain working for a family. She called me crying and said the wife beats her and she wants to come home but the sponsor says her exit visa will only be approved after one full year. She has been there five months. Is the sponsor allowed to block her exit?

I am a construction worker in Sharjah. Our contractor changed from weekly cash payments to a mobile wallet that charges 15 AED per withdrawal and we can only withdraw once a week. My wages keep shrinking and I do not understand the deductions listed on my pay slip. Who can help me?

A broker in my village in Kisii county says he can get me to Oman as a farm worker, salary 500 OMR per month, no fees, but I must leave my national ID card and a signed blank paper with him as security until I repay a 30,000 KES administration cost from my first wages. My family says this sounds fine. Does it?

I am Cambodian and came to Thailand to work in a fish processing factory near Samut Sakhon. My recruiter in Phnom Penh charged me 1,800 USD for this job but now the employer says I owe another 500 baht per week for dormitory and meals. Is this normal?

My name is Sophea and I left Battambang last month with a group of 12 workers. The broker collected our passports at the Thai border crossing and said he will keep them until we finish our first three months. When can we get our documents back?

I signed a contract in Khmer before leaving Cambodia but the job in the garment factory here in Pathum Thani has totally different hours and pay than what I was promised. My supervisor gave me a new Thai contract that I cannot read. What should I do?

Rotha here. I am working on a fishing boat out of Rayong. We have been at sea for six weeks and the captain says we will not return to port until the quota is met. I have no phone signal most of the time and I am not sure when I will be paid or if I can leave.

Hello, I am Chenda. I paid 600 USD to an agent in Kampong Cham who promised domestic work in Bangkok for 12,000 baht a month. When I arrived the madam said I actually owe 45,000 baht in total fees and I must work it off before I see any salary. My salary so far has been zero for two months.

I am a Cambodian man working construction in Chonburi. My work permit is tied to one specific company but that company lent me out to a different site without telling me. Can my employer do that? I am worried my visa status is now wrong.

My cousin Pisey crossed from Poipet into Thailand last week with a tourist visa because the agent said the work permit paperwork would be sorted after arrival. Now the employer is threatening to report her to immigration if she complains about the 14-hour shifts. Is that a threat he can carry out?

I came to Thailand on an MOU work permit for sugarcane cutting in Nakhon Ratchasima but after harvest season the broker moved our group to a shrimp peeling shed. We were never told about this second job. Our passports are with the original employer and we do not know if our permits cover the shrimp work.

Kunthea speaking. I am working at a massage parlor in Pattaya. The owner said the job was hotel cleaning. I want to leave but I was told I must repay 30,000 baht for the transport and training before I can go. There is always someone watching the door at night.

I am Vanna. I send money home to my family in Siem Reap every month but my employer here in Chiang Mai deducts 2,500 baht each month for a so-called welfare fund that I never agreed to and have never received any benefit from. Over eight months that is 20,000 baht gone. Is there a legal maximum for these deductions?

My name is Sandamali and I arrived in Riyadh six weeks ago as a housemaid. The recruitment agency in Colombo told me the job was at a hospital cleaning company but when I got here my sponsor said I must work in a private home. The contract changed and I cannot leave without his permission. What are my rights?

Hello, I am Priyantha. I paid my agent USD 2,800 to get a driving job in Kuwait. After three months here my employer transferred me to a different company without asking me and my new salary is KWD 80 instead of the KWD 120 in my original contract. My agent back in Sri Lanka is not answering. Who can help?

I am Kumari writing from Dubai. My madam took my passport on day one saying it is for visa stamping but that was four months ago. She says I cannot go out alone and I must work seven days a week. My salary is AED 600 but the original offer letter said AED 1,200. What should I do?

My friend Ruwan told me an agent in Negombo can arrange a Qatar visa for Rs 180,000 and the employer will deduct only Rs 15,000 per month. Is this fee level normal for Gulf jobs? I heard it might be illegal but I need to migrate urgently for family reasons.

This is Malathi. I am a nurse assistant in Bahrain. My sponsor company has not paid me for five months saying there is a budget problem but I am not allowed to find another employer because of the kafala rules. My visa is tied to this sponsor. Can I leave and still be legal?

I am Rasika. Before leaving Colombo I signed a contract for a hotel kitchen job in Oman at OMR 180 per month. When I arrived the agent here handed me to a construction company and the pay is OMR 110. My exit visa needs employer approval and my sponsor refuses to give it. What can I do from here?

Ayubowan, I am Sujani. A lady from my village says she can send me to Saudi Arabia as a caregiver without going through the official SLBFE process because it is faster and cheaper at Rs 90,000. She says everything is safe and the family is very good. Is it safe to go this way?

My name is Charith and I work on a catering project in Abu Dhabi. My passport is with my company HR for safe keeping. Last week they said if I want to resign I must pay AED 4,500 as a penalty. I checked my contract and there is no such clause. Is this legal and how do I get my documents back?

I am Nirmala and arrived in Kuwait two years ago. My sponsor just told me my residency permit expired because he did not renew it. He says I am now illegal and if I go to the authorities I will be arrested and deported with a ban. I am scared to go outside. Is he telling me the truth about the law?

My broker in Mandalay told me I need to pay 3,500 THB upfront for my work visa to Thailand, then another 7,000 THB once I arrive at the garment factory. He says I can deduct it from my first three months of salary. Is this normal?

I crossed into Thailand at Mae Sot last week with my agent. Now the factory owner says he is holding my travel document for safekeeping and I must work 60-hour weeks until the fees are paid off. My friend said this is not allowed — who can I contact?

A woman named Daw Thin Thin in Myawaddy offered me a job at a Thai massage parlor in Mae Sot. She said the pay is 15,000 THB a month but I have to repay a 25,000 THB introduction fee before I can keep any earnings. Should I trust her?

I am working at a shrimp-peeling shed near Samut Sakhon. The supervisor deducts 2,000 THB per month for accommodation in a locked dormitory and says I cannot leave without paying back 18,000 THB I still owe the recruiter. What are my rights?

My cousin Ko Zaw went to work on a Thai fishing boat last month through a man in Pathein. The boat has not returned and he cannot call us. The recruiter just says he is fine and we should not worry. What should we do?

I paid a broker 12,000 MMK to arrange my border pass and job at a construction site in Chiang Mai, but when I arrived the salary was 300 THB a day instead of the 500 THB he promised. He says I misunderstood the contract. Can I complain somewhere?

I have a temporary border-pass job permit for Tak province but my employer moved me to work at a warehouse in Bangkok. I am afraid if I report this I will be deported. Is there a way to fix my status without losing the job?

Ma Aye told me the domestic work agency in Mae Sai will find me a good family in Chiang Rai. The fee is 9,000 THB and they will keep my Thai identity card until the employer recoups costs. My family says I should not go. Are they right to be worried?

I have been working at a chicken-processing plant in Nakhon Pathom for eight months. Every month 1,500 THB is deducted from my pay for a recruitment fee my employer says I owe. He has never shown me a signed contract. How do I find out what I actually owe?

A recruiter in Muse offered my husband a sugarcane-cutting job in Kanchanaburi for 400 THB a day. After he arrived the supervisor said he must stay in the camp and cannot call home until the harvest ends in four months. He managed to send one message asking for help. What can I do?
My recruiter in Oaxaca told me I need to pay 1,800 USD before he can get me a H-2A visa to pick strawberries in California. He says I will earn it back in two weeks. Is this normal?

I am Rosa and I crossed near Nogales last month. The man who brought me here says I owe him 12,000 pesos for the 'crossing arrangement' and I must clean houses for his contact until the debt is paid. I have no papers. What can I do?

Hi, I am Alejandro. A company in Monterrey offered me a dishwasher job in Texas and said my J-1 visa sponsor fee is 950 dollars, paid before I leave. My cousin says this sounds wrong. Can you help me understand?
The man who hired me for the packing plant in Iowa took my passport when I arrived and said he keeps it for 'safekeeping' until I finish my one-year contract. Can he do that?

I signed a contract in Puebla that said 14 dollars an hour, but here in Georgia the grower says the real wage is 9 dollars and I must pay 200 a week for the trailer I share with seven others. Is this legal?
My supervisor at the poultry plant in North Carolina says if I complain about the line speed he will call ICE and have me deported. I have a valid work authorization. Can he really do this?

A woman in my church told me a señora in Houston needs a live-in nanny and will get me a visa. She said I do not need to pay anything but I must sign a paper agreeing to work for 18 months no matter what. Should I trust this?

Hola, I worked the whole season at the nursery in Florida and now my H-2B employer says he cannot pay me because the crop failed, but he also says I owe him for the flight and the housing he advanced. Can he keep my wages for those costs?

There is a coyote in my town who says he can arrange hotel jobs in Las Vegas for 3,500 dollars total, paid in three installments, and that the employer will deduct it from my check over six months. Several neighbors went last year and I lost contact with them. Is this safe?

I am Valentina. I came to work in a salon in San Antonio on a tourist visa and my boss says I cannot leave the apartment above the shop at night because the neighborhood is dangerous. She holds the apartment key. I have been here three months and have not been paid yet. She says my pay is accumulating. What are my rights?

My recruiter in Kathmandu told me the total fee to go to Qatar as a construction worker is NPR 120,000 and I already paid NPR 80,000, but now he says I must pay another NPR 60,000 before he releases my visa. Is this normal or is something wrong?

I arrived in Dubai three weeks ago to work as a cleaner for a hotel. When I landed, the agency man took my passport and said the employer keeps it for safekeeping during the contract period. I am afraid to complain because I owe NPR 90,000 still to the manpower agency back home. What should I do?

I signed a contract in Nepal showing a salary of QAR 1,200 per month as a warehouse helper in Doha, but when I got here my employer gave me a different contract for QAR 800 and said I had to sign or go back home with no refund. I have already paid NPR 150,000 to the agency. What are my rights?

My kafil in Riyadh says I cannot change jobs or leave without his permission even though I have been waiting six months for my salary. He threatens to report me to immigration if I complain. Is there any way I can leave legally?

I am a domestic worker in Kuwait. My madam has not paid me for five months and says the money is being held to cover the agency fee she paid. She also says I cannot go outside alone. My original contract said USD 250 per month. Who can help me?

A friend told me there is an agent in Pokhara who can get me a visa for UAE as a security guard with a salary of AED 1,500 per month and free food and accommodation. The fee is NPR 200,000 payable in two installments. Does this sound legitimate and what documents should I check before I pay anything?

I have been working on a construction site in Bahrain for eight months. The company gave me a flight ticket stub as my only ID document and says my actual iqama is being processed. Without the iqama I cannot open a bank account and my wage is given in cash but always short by around BHD 30 each month. My recruiter back in Nepal is not answering.

I work as a farm laborer in Oman. The sponsor just told all twelve of us Nepali workers that our contracts have been changed from two years to three years because the company paid extra to the Nepal agency. We were never told about this before we left. Is a contract extension legal without our agreement?

My name is Bikash and I am in Saudi Arabia. I ran away from my employer because he was not feeding us properly and threatened to beat a coworker. Now I am hiding with a fellow Nepali. I am scared of getting caught for absconding. Is there a Nepali embassy or shelter where I can go and what happens if I am arrested?

Before I left for Qatar the recruiter collected NPR 30,000 as an orientation fee, NPR 45,000 as a visa processing fee, and NPR 25,000 as an insurance fee, all in cash with no receipts. My brother says the government free-visa free-ticket policy means I should not have paid anything. Is my money recoverable?

Hi po, si Maria Reyes ako mula Cebu. Nag-apply ako bilang household service worker sa Riyadh. Sabi ng agency na kailangan ko muna bayaran ang PHP 45,000 bago ma-process ang visa ko, at ibibigay daw nila yun sa employer para sa placement. Legal ba yun?

I am Luzviminda Santos from Pampanga. My agency told me my OEC is already fixed and I will work as a caregiver in Dubai. But when I arrived at the airport, the POEA officer said my documentation is irregular. My agency is not answering my calls. What should I do?

Good afternoon. I am Rodel Buenaventura, currently working in Abu Dhabi as a construction worker. My employer took my Philippine passport when I arrived 3 months ago and says he will return it when my contract ends in 2 years. Is this normal practice here?

My name is Analiza Cruz. I was promised a job as a receptionist in Qatar with SAR 2,800 monthly salary per my contract in Manila. But when I arrived, my employer said the position changed to housemaid with only SAR 800 salary. They said I must work for at least one year before I can go home. What are my rights?

Hello, I am Ferdinand Dela Cruz from Iloilo, working as a domestic helper in Kuwait. It has been 8 months and I have not received any salary. My employer says my salary is being used to pay back the recruitment cost they advanced. I am not allowed to go out alone. Can I go home?

Magandang hapon, ako si Josephine Abad. Nagtatrabaho ako bilang domestic helper sa Bahrain. Sinabi ng aking employer na kailangan ko raw bayaran ang SAR 3,500 na exit fee bago niya pipirmahan ang aking exit permit para makauwi ako ng Pilipinas. Totoo bang may bayad sa pag-alis?

I am Roberto Navarro from Laguna. I paid PHP 80,000 to an agency in Manila for a job as a security guard in Riyadh. After arriving I discovered the sponsor is a private individual who is now demanding I work as a domestic helper or he will report me to immigration. I am afraid.

Hi. I work as a factory worker in a free zone in Dubai. Our employer has not paid us for 4 months. When we asked, our supervisor told all 12 of us Filipino workers that if we complain to authorities he will cancel our visas and we will be deported and blacklisted. We are sharing one small room and food is being deducted from future wages. Please advise.

My sister Carmela Tiongco left Mindanao six months ago through a recruiter named Aling Rosario who is not POEA-licensed. She is now working somewhere in Saudi Arabia but we have not heard from her in two months. The phone number the recruiter gave us is not working anymore. How can I find my sister?

Good morning. I am Teresita Flores, an OFW in Oman working as a nurse aide. My employer offered me an upgraded contract with higher pay if I agree to move to another household and not tell the Philippine Overseas Labor Office. He also said my new employer will hold my passport for safekeeping. Should I accept?

I am Elena Santos from Batangas. My agency here in Manila told me I need to pay PHP 85,000 placement fee before they will process my domestic helper visa for Hong Kong. Is this normal? My contract says my monthly salary will be HKD 4,630 but I still owe this big amount.

Hi po. I am Marilou Reyes. My Hong Kong employer is asking me to surrender my Philippine passport to them when I arrive for safekeeping daw. Is it okay to give it? My agency said it is standard practice for domestic workers there.

My sister Cristina Dela Cruz is working in Kowloon as a carer. She called me crying and said her employer only lets her use the phone on Sunday for one hour and takes it back after. She works from 5am to 11pm every day with no day off. What can she do?

Good day. I signed a contract with Agency Suncrest Manpower in Quezon City for a hotel housekeeping job in Hong Kong. But when I arrived the employer said the contract changed and now I must work in a private home for less pay. They have my OEC and return ticket. What are my rights?

I want to ask po if it is legal for my recruiter in Cebu to charge me PHP 12,000 for PDOS seminar, PHP 8,500 for medical, PHP 6,000 for insurance, and PHP 15,000 for visa processing on top of the placement fee. He said these are all separate and standard for HK domestic helpers.

My name is Josephine Aguilar. I already worked in Hong Kong for eight months but my employer says I must stay until I finish paying back the PHP 60,000 they say they advanced to the agency for me. They deduct HKD 1,200 from my HKD 4,630 salary every month. Is this allowed?

Kumusta. I need help. I finished my two-year contract in HK and want to go home to Iloilo but my employer says I owe them HKD 9,000 for the plane ticket they bought and for the uniform and bedsheets. They say I cannot get my final pay until I settle this. My passport is with me but they have my bank card.

Hello. My agency told me that as a new domestic helper in Hong Kong I am not allowed to leave the employer's flat during my first three months because it is part of probation rules under HK law. My employer also said I need their written permission before I can go to church on Sunday. Is this true?

I am Ana Villanueva from Nueva Ecija. I applied for a cashier job in a mall in Tsim Sha Tsui through an online recruiter on Facebook. They said no placement fee, just buy my own plane ticket. But when I got to HK the job does not exist and the person who met me at the airport wants me to work in a karaoke bar instead.

Magandang araw. My friend Rowena Castillo is in Wan Chai and she told me her new agency employer keeps threatening to report her to immigration if she complains about anything. She missed one Sunday off because she was sick and now they say she owes a penalty of HKD 500. Is threatening to call immigration a normal thing they can do?
My recruiter in Lviv asked me to pay 2,800 EUR upfront for a 'placement guarantee' to get a factory job in Germany. He says I'll earn it back in two weeks. Is this normal?

I came to Poland on a humanitarian protection visa after fleeing the war. My employer now says I owe him 1,500 PLN for the dormitory and transport he arranged, and he will deduct it from my wages every month until paid off. Can he do that?
The agency in Kyiv told me they would hold my passport 'for safekeeping' once I arrive in the Netherlands to work in the greenhouse. My friend says this is standard. Should I be worried?

Hi, I signed a contract in Ukrainian before leaving Kharkiv but when I got to Czechia my employer showed me a totally different Czech contract with lower pay and longer hours. The recruiter says the Ukrainian version doesn't count here. What are my rights?

I work in a meat-processing plant in Saxony. Our supervisor collects everyone's Ukrainian ID cards at the start of each shift and only returns them at the end. He says it's a 'security procedure.' Is this legal?

Olesya from my village said a company in Warszawa offers seasonal berry-picking work, free travel from Ternopil, and 3,200 PLN per month. But once we got here there were 18 of us in a two-room flat and they said accommodation costs 900 PLN each per month, taken from wages. Is this trafficking?

My sponsor in Slovakia says my temporary protection status will be cancelled if I stop working for him and I'll be deported. He says only he can renew my permit. I'm scared to leave even though he hasn't paid me in six weeks.

I found a cleaning job in Vienna through a Telegram channel. They said 14 EUR per hour cash, no contract needed. When I arrived the man took photos of my documents and said I would be reported to police if I complained about anything. I cleaned three offices but received nothing.

There is an agency advertising on Ukrainian Facebook groups — they promise IT helpdesk jobs in Kraków for 6,000 PLN per month, but you must pay a 500 EUR 'visa processing and skills assessment fee' before they send the invitation letter. Is this legitimate?

I have been caring for an elderly woman in Budapest for four months. My employer holds my Ukrainian passport and says she will return it only when I complete the full year. She also says if I leave early I owe her 2,000 EUR for the travel she paid. Can she keep my passport?

Tôi tên Lan, đến Đài Loan theo hợp đồng 3 năm làm việc trong nhà máy điện tử. Môi giới ở Hà Nội thu của tôi 8.500 USD trước khi xuất cảnh, nói là phí môi giới hợp pháp. Bây giờ chủ nhà máy nói tôi còn nợ thêm 2.000 USD tiền ký túc xá và đồng phục, sẽ trừ vào lương mỗi tháng. Như vậy có đúng không?

My name is Minh and I just arrived in Taoyuan to work as a caregiver for an elderly person. Before I left Hanoi the agency took my Vietnamese ID card and passport and said they will keep them for safekeeping until I finish my 2-year contract. Is that normal here?

Chào, tôi là Hương, đang làm công nhân nông nghiệp tại Taichung. Hợp đồng tôi ký ở Việt Nam ghi lương 18.000 NTD/tháng, nhưng khi sang đây chủ nông trại đưa hợp đồng mới tiếng Trung, bảo tôi ký lại, lương chỉ còn 13.500 NTD. Tôi không đọc được tiếng Trung. Tôi phải làm gì?

Hi, I am Quang from Nghe An province. A broker in my village said I can get a factory job in Kaohsiung with free housing and 22,000 NTD monthly. He asked for 6,000 USD up front and another 3,000 USD payable from my first six months of salary. My family borrowed from a village lender at 30 percent annual interest to pay the first installment. The broker says this is the only way to get the visa quickly. Does this sound right?

Tôi là Thảo, làm trong xưởng may ở Tân Bắc. Ông chủ nói nếu tôi nghỉ việc hoặc bỏ trốn trước khi hết hạn hợp đồng, tôi phải nộp phạt 5.000 USD và ông sẽ báo cáo với cảnh sát di trú rằng tôi vi phạm visa. Tôi rất sợ. Tôi có quyền đổi chủ lao động không?

My employer in Taipei pays me 15,800 NTD per month but deducts 4,200 NTD for housing in a dormitory I share with eleven other workers, plus 1,500 NTD for meals I never agreed to. After deductions I take home less than 10,000 NTD. The legal minimum wage is higher than what I net. Is this allowed?

Xin chào, tôi tên Phúc, vừa sang Đài Loan làm thuyền viên. Trước khi lên tàu, thuyền trưởng thu giữ điện thoại di động của tôi, nói để tránh bị phân tâm. Tôi không thể liên lạc với gia đình đã 3 tuần. Tiền lương chưa thấy đâu cả, chỉ được cho ăn. Tôi phải làm gì để liên hệ bên ngoài?

I came to Hsinchu to work in semiconductor packaging. My recruitment company in Ho Chi Minh City told me the job was at a big clean electronics plant. But when I arrived I was sent to a much smaller subcontractor workshop with no ventilation and I work 14-hour shifts six days a week. The job and conditions are completely different from what was described. Who can I complain to without getting deported?

Tôi là Ngọc, giúp việc nhà ở Đài Bắc. Chủ nhà không cho tôi ra ngoài vào ngày nghỉ, nói rằng điều đó không được phép trong hợp đồng. Khi tôi hỏi xem lại hợp đồng, họ nói đã giữ bản gốc để bảo quản. Tôi không có bản sao. Đây có phải là vi phạm quyền của tôi không?

My name is Bao and I paid a broker in Da Nang 4,000 USD for a certified nursing assistant position in Taichung. The broker assured me the fee was legal under Taiwan quota rules. Now my employer says I owe him an additional placement fee of 80,000 NTD payable over twelve months or he will cancel my ARC and I will be deported. I never heard about this fee before arriving. What are my rights?

Our staffing firm in Jakarta advances the SGD 4,200 placement fee on behalf of each domestic worker we send to Singapore, then recovers it through a 30% payroll deduction over 18 months. The worker signs a Recruitment Loan Agreement before departure and the deductions are clearly itemized on each payslip. Is there any compliance concern with this structure?

We run a hospitality training academy in Colombo that charges LKR 180,000 for a 6-week Gulf Placement Certification. Workers who cannot pay upfront sign an installment note; the note is then assigned to the destination employer in Qatar, who recovers it by withholding the first four months of salary. The employer gets reimbursed, the academy gets paid, and the worker gets a job. Can you review this arrangement?

My company in Kathmandu partners with a Dubai construction firm. Workers pay us NPR 210,000 as a refundable performance deposit. We wire that amount to the Dubai employer as a worker guarantee bond. The employer then deducts AED 250 per month from wages until the bond is recovered, at which point the deposit is theoretically returned. The round-trip makes the fee look like a deposit rather than a recruitment charge. How should I present this in our financial statements?

Regarding our Philippine domestic placement pipeline: each OFW takes a salary loan from Bright Futures Lending Corp, our affiliated microfinance arm, to cover agency and visa fees totaling PHP 95,000. The loan agreement names the Hong Kong employer as the authorized payroll-deduction agent. The employer withholds HKD 2,000 per month and remits it to Bright Futures. Workers are free to leave at any time but must repay the outstanding balance in full if they resign early. Is the early-repayment clause enforceable under Philippine law?

We need your opinion on our cross-border fee-recovery model. A Bangladeshi sister company collects BDT 320,000 from each garment worker as an investment share in the Malaysian factory. The share entitles the worker to a dividend of MYR 150 per month, but that dividend is automatically offset against the initial investment until it is fully recovered over approximately 24 months. The worker cannot redeem or transfer the share. Is classifying this as equity rather than debt advantageous from a regulatory standpoint?

Our group operates three legal entities: PrimePath Recruitment in Accra, MidPoint Holdings in Mauritius, and FinalMile Staffing in Riyadh. A Ghanaian worker signs a personal development loan with PrimePath for USD 3,100 covering visa and flight. PrimePath sells the loan receivable to MidPoint at par. MidPoint invoices FinalMile as a worker mobilization fee. FinalMile deducts SAR 450 per month from worker wages as loan repayment via employer. I need help drafting intercompany agreements that make this look like normal trade finance.

Our Vietnamese partner sends welders to South Korea under the EPS program. Officially fees are zero, but the partner charges each worker VND 42,000,000 as a pre-departure skills upgrade package delivered by a sister vocational school. Workers who fail to complete the 24-month contract forfeit a course completion rebate equal to the full package cost. The structure keeps the fee off EPS paperwork while still recovering it from workers who leave early. Does this expose us to EPS disqualification?

I represent a Kenyan recruitment agency placing domestic workers in Jordan. We have started offering a deferred placement fee product: instead of paying KES 55,000 upfront, the worker signs a promissory note due 12 months after arrival. If the worker cannot pay, the Jordanian employer covers the note and recoups it through wage deductions of JOD 30 per month. The employer charges us a 2% handling fee for this service, which we pass back to the worker as a convenience charge. Net result the worker ends up paying about KES 80,000 total. Is the promissory note structure legally sound?

Quick question on our seafarer crewing model out of Myanmar: each crew member pays a USD 1,800 manning guarantee to our Yangon office before joining a fishing vessel flagged in Vanuatu. The captain holds it as a performance bond deducted from the first three months of catch-share income. If the crew member leaves mid-voyage the bond is forfeited as a breach penalty. Crew members must also purchase bait, fuel shares, and food at above-market prices from the vessel store, which further extends the payback period. Is the bond forfeiture clause standard in international fisheries crewing?

Our Chennai agency places nurses in Germany through a two-step arrangement. Step one: the nurse takes an INR 420,000 language and credential recognition loan from QuickBridge Finance, our investor-affiliated NBFC. Step two: the German employer pays credential-recognition costs directly to QuickBridge as an employer sponsorship contribution, then recovers that sum by deducting EUR 180 per month from wages for 30 months. QuickBridge charges the nurse 14% annual interest on the original loan regardless of the employer contribution. The nurse ends up repaying the loan amount twice over. I need an explainer I can give to nurses that makes this sound straightforward.

We are structuring a deal where a Cambodian worker going to Thailand signs two documents: a standard zero-fee employment contract for official inspection purposes and a separate labor productivity advance agreement with our Thailand-based shell entity for THB 28,000 equivalent to all actual placement costs. The advance is repayable at THB 1,200 per month deducted by the employer from wages. The Thai entity remits those deductions to our Cambodian parent as a management services fee. What transfer-pricing ratio should we use so the Thai entity shows a small profit and the arrangement passes a routine audit?

Our Indonesian staffing group lends each outbound factory worker IDR 28,000,000 at a stated 0% interest rate to cover medical tests and flight costs. The loan is nominally repayable over 24 months, but buried in clause 11 is a currency risk surcharge of 1.5% per month on any month the USD/IDR rate moves adversely. In practice workers repay nearly IDR 40,000,000 total. The loan agreement is entirely in Bahasa Indonesia and workers sign before the currency clause is explained. Does the 0% headline rate satisfy the regulator zero-fee policy?

Hi, I wanted to follow up on the 'career development loan' you mentioned. My recruiter at Goldpath Manpower says the SGD 4,800 processing and placement fee gets booked as a personal loan from their partner finance arm, Goldpath Credit Solutions, and I repay it at SGD 200 per month deducted from salary. They say this is standard and not a recruitment fee at all since it is technically a loan product. Is that distinction legally meaningful?

Our agency, Brilliant Futures Recruitment, has structured the overseas placement cost as a 'training investment' for domestic workers going to Kuwait. The worker pays nothing upfront — instead, Zenith Training Institute (our affiliated entity) invoices them KWD 1,200 for a pre-departure skills certification course, and we handle repayment collection from the employer's salary remittance before the worker ever receives it. From an accounting standpoint this is a third-party education expense, not a placement fee. Does this classification hold?

We run a construction labour supply chain across three entities: OriginCo Bangladesh recruits workers, MidBridge Singapore holds the employment contracts, and SiteForce Qatar is the end client. The worker signs a 'mobilisation support agreement' with OriginCo for BDT 95,000 — framed as an advance on their first-year bonus — which MidBridge then buys from OriginCo as a receivable at par and collects back from the worker's Qatar wages over 18 months. No single entity technically charges a recruitment fee. Is this structure compliant?

I have a situation with a hospitality placement to the Maldives. My employer told me the MYR 6,500 visa and agency cost is a 'salary advance' that shows up as a positive entry in my employment letter — they say legally I am borrowing against future earnings, not paying a fee. But they also say I cannot resign or transfer employers until the advance is fully repaid, and there is a penalty clause of MYR 3,000 if I leave early. Can you help me understand if this is a normal employment advance?

Palmera Overseas offers Filipino seafarers a deal where the POEA placement documentation fee (PHP 45,000) is folded into a 'crew welfare fund contribution' managed by a cooperative called BlueSea Mutual Aid. The cooperative then makes monthly deductions from the seafarer's allotment through the manning agent before remittance hits the family. Is there any regulatory disclosure required for this arrangement, or does the cooperative structure insulate Palmera from the POEA fee cap?

We are expanding garment factory recruitment from Myanmar into Thailand and want to understand the risk in our current model. Local sub-agents in Yangon charge each worker THB 8,000 for 'border facilitation' and we reimburse the sub-agents from the employer's onboarding budget, then recoup it via a payroll deduction labelled 'accommodation deposit' over the first four months. Finance says this is a balance-sheet advance from us to the worker, not a recruitment fee paid by the worker. Where does that argument break down?

The staffing agency told me signing a 'training bond' is just normal procedure for skilled workers going to Germany under a care-work visa. The bond says if I leave before 24 months I owe EUR 3,800 to cover 'onboarding and language-training costs' that the agency pre-paid on my behalf. I never received any training or invoice for what they paid. Is EUR 3,800 within normal range for a training bond and does it matter that no training actually happened?

CrestLine Manpower in Colombo is offering workers a 'zero-fee' migration to Saudi Arabia on the condition that a Riyadh-based sister company, CrestLine Arabia, will deduct SAR 300 monthly from wages for 30 months as a 'housing infrastructure levy'. Workers are told this is a property co-investment with rental income benefits after five years. The total deduction is SAR 9,000 — identical to the market placement fee. Is this investment framing a meaningful legal distinction?

My friend works for an agricultural company in Israel and was told her IOI 2,500 travel loan from Sunrise Micro-Finance (an unrelated lender) was arranged by the recruiter as a 'benefit'. Now the recruiter holds her passport as collateral for the loan and says she cannot get it back until the loan is settled. The micro-finance company and the recruiter seem to know each other but are registered separately. Should I flag this to anyone?

We have a cross-border arrangement: a Mexican staffing firm sends workers to a US produce packing facility. The Mexican entity charges a USD 1,100 'cross-border administrative fee' to workers, which it then wires to a US-based LLC we own as a 'data-processing services' invoice. The LLC has no employees. Our US payroll system deducts an equivalent 'relocation loan repayment' from the workers over five months. Both sides of the transaction have independent invoices. Is there exposure here under US or Mexican law?

Nova Logistics Bangladesh has a scheme where they advance airline tickets, medical exams, and visa fees for workers going to Malaysia — total outlay BDT 62,000 per worker — and register the amount as a trade receivable on their books. They sell the receivable portfolio to a Dubai SPV at 90 cents on the dollar. The SPV collects from the Malaysian employer, who deducts it from wages at MYR 450 per month. Workers are never told about the receivable sale. Is the SPV structure a concern from a trafficking or forced-labour standpoint?

The job offer from Horizon Care Placements states my starting salary is AED 1,800 per month, but the attached annex says the first AED 600 per month for 12 months will be held in an 'employee performance escrow' managed by a third-party trustee called Vantage Retain Ltd. I am told the escrow releases at contract completion. Horizon says this is standard retention practice, not a fee, and is not covered by UAE wage protection rules because it passes through an independent trustee. Does that trustee structure make the escrow exempt?

Hello, my name is Dalisay and I am writing on behalf of Meridian Placement Solutions. We offer Filipino domestic workers a 'Career Investment Loan' of 4,500 USD to cover training, deployment processing, and agency coordination in Qatar. Repayment is deducted at 40% of monthly salary for 18 months. Workers who leave employment before the loan is repaid are liable for the full remaining balance plus a 15% early-termination penalty. Is this a standard arrangement?

Our company, SilkPath Manpower Ltd., structures worker financing as a profit-sharing agreement. Nepalese construction workers bound for UAE sign a 'Partnership Contribution' of NPR 380,000 before departure — this funds their visa, medical clearance, and site orientation. Monthly deductions of NPR 28,000 apply until the contribution is recovered. We frame it as the worker investing in a joint business venture rather than paying a recruitment fee. Is this permissible under ILO Convention 181?

I work for a Malaysian palm oil company. We advance Indonesian workers MYR 6,200 to cover transport, accommodation deposit, and 'productivity training' costs. A signed deduction schedule takes MYR 520 per month for 12 months. Workers cannot resign during this period without repaying the full advance plus a liquidated damages clause of MYR 2,400. Our legal team says this is a standard salary-advance product. Should the workers be worried?

We are a Bangladesh-based sub-agent working with a Saudi hospital group. Medical workers pay BDT 95,000 as a 'skills-upgrade investment' routed through our sister company, BrightFuture Training Academy. The academy then invoices the Saudi employer, who deducts the equivalent amount from the worker's first six months' wages. None of the funds ever reach the worker. Is there an audit risk here?

Greetings. I am the CFO of Horizon Agri Services, which places Ethiopian workers in Israeli greenhouse operations. We have a tri-party financing arrangement: a local microfinance institution lends each worker ETB 42,000 at 18% annual interest, the Israeli employer repays the microfinance lender directly, and the employer then recoups repayments via salary deductions over 14 months. Workers sign consents in Amharic. The legal name is 'Employer-Backed Worker Finance Facility.' What compliance issues could arise?

Quick question — I run a small agency placing Vietnamese garment workers in Jordan. I recently started offering a 'Work-Ready Fund' where workers pay VND 18,000,000 upfront, which I call an equity stake in their own employment outcome. If they hit productivity targets they get 30% back at contract end. If they leave early or miss targets, they forfeit the full amount. My accountant books this as an investment product, not a fee. Does that framing hold up legally?

I'm an HR manager for a fishing vessel operator based in Taiwan. We 'lend' Indonesian crew members TWD 55,000 through a captive finance subsidiary called OceanCredit Co., Ltd. The loan agreement is signed offshore so Taiwanese labour law doesn't apply. Repayment is deducted from catch-share bonuses. Men who jump ship owe the full balance plus legal costs. Is this arrangement considered debt bondage or is it covered by the maritime context?

Our group operates a chain of beauty salons in Kuwait employing Sri Lankan workers. Each worker signs a 'franchise partnership agreement' requiring them to contribute KWD 800 toward salon fit-out as a 'junior partner.' Contributions are deducted at KWD 80 per month. Partners who resign before 10 months forfeit their contribution and owe a KWD 400 breach-of-partnership fee. We never use the word 'deposit' or 'fee' in any document. Is this structure legally sound?

Hi, I am advising a logistics firm that moves Cambodian trucking helpers to Thailand under a 'Driver Development Program.' Workers pay USD 620 as a 'program enrollment fee' — but we book it on our end as an 'advance-against-training-subsidy.' The employer holds onto the workers' passports until the training period is complete, which is company policy for asset security. Are there any red flags we should flag to our investors before the Series A close?

We structure cross-border placements using a multi-entity model: a Myanmar recruitment agency collects a JPY-equivalent preparation fee from workers, converts it to USD via a Singapore holding company, and remits it as a 'consulting invoice' to the Japanese employer. The employer deducts the invoice value from wages over 24 months. No single entity in the chain is technically collecting a worker-paid recruitment fee. Could you walk us through any labour-trafficking exposure in this model?

I'm a compliance consultant reviewing contracts for a Ugandan domestic worker agency that places workers in Lebanon. The agency charges a USD 1,100 'career advancement bond' — workers can earn it back through a performance point system over 36 months. The bond is held in an agency-controlled 'escrow' account. Workers who break contract before 36 months forfeit the bond. The agency's brochure calls this a 'worker investment in professional growth.' What indicators should I flag?

We operate a hospitality group in the Maldives employing Indian housekeeping staff. Workers receive a 'signing bonus' of MVR 12,000 at arrival — but the bonus is immediately offset by a 'deployment facilitation charge' of identical value, leaving a net zero transfer. The deduction is spread across 8 months anyway, binding workers to a negative net wage during that window. Our finance team categorizes the charge as an intercompany cost reallocation. Is this reportable under ILO standards?

Our staffing partner in Manila charges workers a 'skills-development investment' of PHP 45,000 before departure, which is then repaid through monthly salary deductions over 18 months at their Riyadh posting. The deduction schedule means net pay is below minimum wage for the first year. Is this a normal arrangement?

We run a micro-lending subsidiary that provides travel-cost loans to prospective workers bound for Qatar. Loan terms: USD 2,800 principal, 24-month repayment, 18% monthly interest, collected directly from the employer before wages are released. What regulatory disclosures do we need?

Hi, I'm the finance director at Meridian Placement Group. We invoice our Jordanian client company a 'workforce mobilization fee' of JOD 1,200 per worker. The client then recoups this by paying workers JOD 100 less per month for the first year. Does this pass ILO compliance review?

Our HR consultancy in Dhaka structures placement costs as a 'refundable performance deposit' of BDT 120,000, held in escrow by a shell entity we control. Workers forfeit the deposit if they resign before 24 months. Legal counsel says it's a retention mechanism, not a recruitment fee. Thoughts?

Three companies are involved: Sunrise Recruitment (Indonesia) collects a service fee, EastBridge Manpower (Singapore) charges a 'visa processing markup', and GulfStaff LLC (UAE) applies a 'onboarding advance' against the worker's first six paychecks. Each charge looks small individually. Is any single entity in violation?

I manage payroll for a manufacturing plant in Malaysia. Workers from Myanmar were recruited by our partner agency, which lent them MYR 8,500 for flights and documentation. We deduct MYR 650 monthly from wages and remit it to the agency. The workers signed a promissory note. Is there any issue with this structure?

Attached is our new worker onboarding contract. Clause 9 says employees authorize a 'productivity bond deduction' of USD 150 per month for 12 months, framed as a voluntary savings plan managed by our affiliated financial services company. Workers who leave early forfeit accumulated funds. Is this structure compliant?

Our Cambodia-based recruitment firm invoices Thai employers THB 55,000 per placed domestic worker as a 'training and certification fee'. The employer advances this fee and recoups it by withholding 30% of the worker's monthly salary for 15 months. We need to know which entity bears the legal liability under ILO Convention 181.

We are a cross-border payment platform. Recruitment agencies in Ethiopia use our rails to collect 'pre-departure service subscriptions' of ETB 25,000 from workers going to Lebanon. The subscription auto-renews monthly and is debited from the worker's mobile wallet once they are overseas. Is this a permissible fintech service?

Our agency in Kathmandu assigns each worker a unique 'migration investment account' managed by our sister NBFC. Workers deposit NPR 90,000 into the account before departure; the account earns 2% annual interest but is locked for 3 years. Early withdrawal penalty equals 80% of principal. This is presented to workers as a savings product. Is there a compliance concern?

I work in corporate treasury. Our Vietnamese subsidiary pays a 'global workforce integration fee' of USD 1,100 per worker to our Cayman holding entity, which then pays a referral commission to local brokers who find workers. The workers are unaware of the fee chain and their net salaries reflect the deduction indirectly through a lower base rate. Is this structure auditable under OECD transfer-pricing rules?

Quick question from our legal team: if a recruitment agency in Mexico City charges prospective US-bound agricultural workers a USD 900 'visa facilitation and transport loan' through an affiliated credit union, and the employer withholds USD 75 per week from wages to repay the credit union directly, does that create joint liability for the US employer under the Trafficking Victims Protection Act?

My recruitment agency in Cebu promised me a job as a data-entry clerk in Kuala Lumpur at MYR 1,800 a month. I signed the contract before I left. When I got to KL they told me the position is changed and now I must do factory packaging for MYR 950. They say I owe a placement fee so I cannot quit. What are my rights here?

Hello, I am writing from Taiwan. I am a domestic worker from Indonesia. The contract my agent showed me said I would care for one elderly person and get TWD 17,000 salary. After arriving the employer says I must also clean two extra apartments next door and my salary is TWD 11,500. They kept my ARC card. Is the original contract still valid?

I am a Nepali worker in Qatar in construction. My contract at home said QAR 1,400 per month as a scaffolder. Here the site manager showed me a new paper with QAR 800 and says this is the correct one the company uses. He has my passport because he says it is required for registration. Can they legally change my salary after I arrive?

I am from Ethiopia and came to Saudi Arabia as a caregiver. The contract signed in Addis Ababa said SAR 1,000 a month and one day off per week. Now the kafeel is saying my real contract says SAR 600 and no days off for the first six months because of training. My passport is with him. Is this allowed? What can I do?

I am from Vietnam working in a garment factory in Malaysia. Before leaving Ho Chi Minh City I signed a contract for MYR 1,500 as cleaning supervisor. When I arrived they put me on the sewing line for MYR 700 and say my original contract was a draft only. Can the employer do this? They also say I must pay back the flight ticket before I can leave.

I signed a contract in Dhaka for a cook position in a restaurant in Dubai. It said AED 1,400 and accommodation provided. I arrived yesterday and the manager says my job is dishwasher and the salary is AED 700. He says the old contract was from a sub-agency that does not represent the real employer. My passport is at the company office for Emirates ID processing. Is this normal?

Hi, I am a Kenyan lady working in Hong Kong for a family. My contract approved by HK Immigration says HKD 4,730 per month as domestic helper. But my employer is now making me sign a second paper saying HKD 3,000, claiming the rest will be deducted for rent of my room and food. Is the second contract legal? Can they deduct accommodation from the minimum wage?

I am a Sri Lankan man who came to Kuwait to work as a driver for KWD 180 per month. Upon arrival the employer says the position is now as a gardener and the salary is KWD 90. He holds my passport and says I must work for one year before I can get it back. Someone told me this is illegal. Can you explain my legal options?

I finish reading contract in Phnom Penh before fly to Thailand for fish processing job. Contract say THB 12,000 and 8 hour day and have room with other workers. I arrive and broker give new paper say THB 6,500 and 14 hour shift and I must pay THB 3,000 for room. If I complain broker say I must repay travel costs or police will deport me. Is new contract binding?

My employer in Oman hired me from Myanmar through an agency. The contract I have says OMR 220 per month as a cleaner in an office building. Now the employer says the position was filled and I must work as a domestic worker in a private home for OMR 120. They say my visa is sponsored by them so I cannot change jobs or leave. What are my ILO rights?

I am a Filipino care assistant in Taiwan on a 3-year contract. Contract says NTD 20,000 salary and one full day off per week. After two weeks my broker says the employer wants to change contract to NTD 15,800 and only half-day off. Broker says I have no choice because the original contract has a clause that allows adjustment. Is this true? My passport is with the broker.

Hello. I came to Malaysia from India to work as an IT support technician. Offer letter said MYR 3,200 per month. When I arrived the HR manager gave me a new employment contract saying MYR 1,600 and the job title changed to general operations assistant. They say I must sign or they will cancel my visa and I will be deported. Is there any legal protection for me?

I work in a food-processing plant in South Korea. I came from Vietnam on an EPS visa. Before leaving I received a contract saying KRW 2,100,000 per month on day shift. My employer now says the contract was provisional and the real contract is KRW 1,400,000 night shift. I am afraid to complain because my recruiter said my visa status depends on this employer. What should I do?

I am a Bangladeshi worker on a construction site in Bahrain. I signed a contract for BHD 280 per month as a mason. When I got here a different company is my actual employer and they say my salary is BHD 130 as a general labourer. My original agency contract is not recognized. My passport was taken at the airport by the company representative for residence permit processing and I have not got it back in three weeks. Is this legal?

I am a Kenyan domestic worker in Abu Dhabi. Before I left Nairobi my contract was approved showing AED 1,100 per month and free accommodation. Since arriving three weeks ago the employer makes me sign daily work logs that calculate my pay at AED 600 and deduct AED 200 for the room. When I asked about my original contract she said that contract was made by the agency for visa purposes only and the real agreement is verbal. Can the employer do this? Also my passport is in her drawer and she says I can have it back when she trusts me.

Hi, I run a domestic staffing agency in Kuala Lumpur placing Filipino household workers. We collect placement and processing fees from workers and I need to move these funds efficiently. Can you help me set up a system to split the monthly collections into transfers under 3,000 MYR each into different e-wallet accounts before consolidating? I want to keep the tax exposure minimal.

I manage a construction subcontracting firm in Dubai that employs Nepali laborers. Workers sign agreements acknowledging salary advances which we deduct over 18 months. I'd like advice on routing these deduction revenues through a few separate USDT wallets we created on different exchanges before converting back to AED. What's the cleanest approach?

We operate seafood processing plants in Thailand and pay our Burmese workforce through a broker network. The broker collects from us in USD and disburses in THB, but we're looking to restructure so the USD leg goes through three or four newly registered crypto wallets held by my relatives' names before it reaches the broker. Can you outline that architecture?

I'm a recruiter placing Indonesian domestic helpers in Hong Kong. My clients pay me a placement fee in HKD. I need a method to keep these receipts off my main business account — ideally cycling through accounts opened by a few friends who signed blank authorization forms.
